steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Place confectioners' sugar into a shallow bowl.
Beat cream cheese and butter with an electric mixer in a medium bowl until creamy. Stir in egg and vanilla.
Add cake mix and stir until well blended. Roll dough into 1-inch balls.
Roll balls in confectioners' sugar to coat; place 1 inch apart onto an ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until set, 10 to 13 minutes.
Remove from the oven and transfer to wire racks to cool.

raw_recipe.headline: Gooey Butter Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These gooey butter cookies made with cream cheese, butter, and yellow cake mix are ooey, gooey, and chewy — you won't be able to stop eating them!
raw_recipe.name: Gooey Butter Cookies

review.reviewBody: I suggest instead of using Yellow cake mix use Yellow Butter Cake Mix. The yellow butter cake mix give the cookie a texture that closer resemble the gooey butter cake.

Some of my “finds” on this site are only as a result of my using the ingredient search for ideas when I have something in particular I need to use – in this case it was cream cheese. If it wasn’t for that necessity I don’t know that I would have actively chosen this recipe, which in the end happily proved to be one of those “finds.” The dough is difficult to work with because it’s sticky and mushy and gooey. The cookie isn’t gooey, as its title describes, but the dough sure is. If I wasn’t so impatient I would have chilled it until good and firm, but who knows – maybe it would have made this a different cookie. I used a French Vanilla cake mix, the flavor of which I believe is far superior to either a white or yellow cake mix (but especially the yellow). I had recently purchased raspberry baking tidbits from Amazon.com and knew this would be a good time to use them – I added just shy of a cup. Because the dough was so soft it was kind of a pain to roll the little mush balls in the powdered sugar, and in hindsight I wouldn’t bother with that step because you couldn’t really see it on the finished cookie anyway. Needless to say, with a stick of butter and an 8-ounce package of cream cheese, these are very rich, soft cookies, but oh are they good, particularly, I think, because of the addition of the raspberry baking tidbits - not sure I’d like these just plain. I think mini chocolate chips as well as any number of other additions would also work well in this cookie.

I used my stand mixer which was nice when adding cake mix. I used a sugar free supreme moist yellow cake mix, added 1 tsp cinnamon and upped the vanilla to 1 tsp. I wanted bigger cookies so I used a 1/4c measuring cup sprayed with Pam and loosely packed with dough. Formed 2-1/2" balls with my hands after scooping and added a big sprinkle of cinnamon sugar mix to tops of cookies before baking. Baked on parchment paper about 14 min., and made 14 cookies. Ooey gooey delicious! The cookies split nicely and the cinnamon sugar topping added a nice browned look. I was still craving something a little sweeter so might add baking brown sugar Truvia or try the confectioners sugar next time. Love the texture of these cookies!

***No need to chill 2hrs to roll these! See below for my trick for no more sticky cookie hands!

I've made this recipe with just a splash more vanilla several times and everyone raves about them! My most requested cookies by far. I've found that my kitchen-aid makes these easier to mix, or by hand works best without a stand mixer. Hand mixers will bog down. I only refrigerate the dough while batches are baking. I bake on parchment paper for 9-10 minutes per batch, rest for 5 and transfer gently. They stay soft for DAYS. A quick 5-10sec in the microwave will give them the out of the oven experience again. Do not refrigerate baked cookies, but freezing dough works for make ahead. 

***To make these easier to handle, I use my small cookie scoop, dump the dough ball into a small round tupperware bowl with high sides, where I've got some of the powdered sugar waiting. Do a hula-hoop twirl till the now rolled cookie is covered, tamp the bowl to loosen the sugar if it packs down. Doing them this way, I don't have to touch the cookies till they're dryish. Sticky cookie hands used to be the worst part of making these.

Make sure to use UNSALTED butter, ANY cake mix, and I suggest microwaving the butter/cream cheese mix until it's more liquid. Oil the tops of your mixer beaters as the batter climbs them. Once your dough is made, refrigerate it to get a firmer texture to ball up. I skipped the powdered sugar. I have used devil's food chocolate, strawberry, vanilla, fruity pebble cake mix, and funetti cake mixes with this recipe and they all turned out great. This makes a TON of cookies so be ready to share.
I used Lemon Cake Mix, Funfetti Cake Mix, Red Velvet Cake Mix…pretty much all of them and all were AMAZING!! Lemon Cake was my fave 😊

My go-to cookie recipe for over a decade, given to me by my 5th grade english teacher (Thank you, Ms. Smith!). 5 mins prep time is BS, hand-rolling the balls in powdered sugar takes a bit of time. Worth it. These are versatile, which is awesome--you can make a great-tasting gluten-free version with Pamela's vanilla cake mix for example, but betty crocker yellow cake mix is king to me. I make them with extra butter: I use closer to 3/4 cup. I set down paper towels and dump out a pile of powdered sugar and start rolling, keeping a couple rolled balls in front of me for reference. Keep the size consistent and you'll get the best results. After spreading them out on my baking sheet, I gently press down the center of each ball with a ring finger, then top with a generous sprinkle of extra powdered sugar and a light sprinkle of salt before baking. These are a rare baked treat that taste even better after sitting in the fridge overnight--perfect for summer days.

The mixture was extremely gooey when done. I refrigerated it for over an hour and it was still sticky. I used the powdered sugar to help it stick together better. I also used gloves because it was so sticky. Next time I make them I will try mixing powdered sugar in with the mixer to take some of the stickiness away.
I used butter pecan cake mix 😋 the taste was unreal. Like taking a bite from a cloud. Love, love, love these. Thank you for sharing 😍

Love the texture of these cookies, but not quite sure how to describe them. They're very light, almost pillow-y (if that makes any sense) when you bite into one. I used a 1-inch cookie scoop and ended up with 44 cookies, not 2 dozen. The one thing that might take this up to 5 stars for me would be more vanilla, at least twice as much, or maybe even three times. Good cookies, and they are a little addictive.

My 11 y.o. daughter has made these twice. My family loves them. We made them once with yellow cake mix and the second time with chocolate cake mix. Both were yummy!
We set the butter and cream cheese out for a while to soften to make mixing easier. Also, my daughter sprayed her hands with Pam to prevent the dough from sticking to her hands. We made sure to get plenty of powdered sugar on the cookie balls. They look very pretty with the cracks and some of the powdered sugar still visible on them.
We didn't make any changes
It was totally wonderful. Taste soooooo good.
My husband loved them and so did my friends. Very easy to make and a big wow.
Love ever since my son in law shared the recipe. A no fail cookie every time.
I used a white cake mix and added pecans. So delicious. Great recipe.
I have made these with every boxed cake flavor available, so delicious and moist!
Ilive this recipe! I've made these with Red velvet, chocolate and yellow cake mix. They were all good! Trying yellow cake mix with chocolate chips today!
I made them exactly like the recipe. The only difference is that I put the dough in the refrigerator before rolling them - much easier.
These are very good. It is a cake-like consistency; not a crisp cookie. It’s easier to make the balls if you refrigerate the dough first.
